meta.note: Slice 1 per Build Spec v1 §2. Core = niches named in the spec; adjacent = contrast niches, approved by Benjamin 2026-10-31 (D-31.9).

niches.name: Rationalists (LessWrong / ACX)
niches.description: A community organized around Bayesian epistemics, cognitive-bias correction and long essays, centered on LessWrong and Astral Codex Ten. It produced much of the early AI-risk analysis and overlaps heavily with EA and with forecasting.

niches.name: AI safety / existential-risk community
niches.description: People who believe advanced AI could cause human extinction or permanent disempowerment, and that the industry race makes this likely without intervention. It ranges from technical alignment researchers to people calling for a global moratorium. The 2025 book 'If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies' and the 'AI 2027' scenario raised its profile.

niches.name: Effective accelerationists (e/acc)
niches.description: An online movement, born in 2022 on X, that treats technological and capital growth as a thermodynamic imperative. It wants to speed AI and other technology up rather than slow it down. Members talk in memes, physics metaphors and builder culture, and see AI-safety regulation as the main obstacle.

niches.name: Techno-optimists / American Dynamism / hard-tech builders
niches.description: Venture capitalists and founders who hold that technology is the main engine of human flourishing and of national strength. Its American Dynamism wing wants to rebuild physical industry, defense and manufacturing in the US. Andreessen's 2023 'Techno-Optimist Manifesto' is its founding text.

niches.name: TPOT / post-rationalists
niches.description: A loose X subculture that grew out of and away from rationalism. It values wisdom, embodiment, vibes, meditation and playful sincerity over strict Bayesianism, and has its own gatherings (Vibecamp) and blogging culture. It sits at the meeting point of tech, meaning-making and contemplative practice.

niches.name: Effective altruists
niches.description: A philanthropic and intellectual movement that tries to do the most good per unit of resources. Its main priorities are global health, animal welfare and, increasingly, reducing catastrophic risk from AI. It rebranded and decentralized after the FTX collapse.

niches.name: Tech right / Silicon Valley New Right
niches.description: The political turn of a section of Silicon Valley toward the Republican right, centered on Peter Thiel's network, the All-In podcast and figures who joined or advised the 2025 Trump administration (JD Vance, David Sacks). It mixes libertarian economics with national-conservative, anti-'woke' and civilizational themes.

niches.name: Degens / memecoin culture
niches.description: Speculative crypto culture organized around memecoins, livestreamed trading and irony. It holds that everything is a casino and the honest move is to play it. Members treat community belief and memes as the real asset ('memecoin supercycle'), and the Remilia / Milady wing adds a net-art, quasi-spiritual layer.

niches.name: AGI frontier-lab builders & AI-progress watchers
niches.description: Leaders, researchers and close observers of the frontier AI labs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI) who expect transformative or general AI within years. They see building it carefully, and first, as the central project of the age. Their views sit between acceleration and safety, and they debate timelines, scaling and governance among themselves.

niches.name: AI ethics / critical AI studies
niches.description: Scholars and advocates who focus on present-day harms of AI: bias, surveillance, labor exploitation, concentration of power and misleading hype. They reject both the utopian and the extinction narratives as distractions that serve the industry. The 2025 book 'The AI Con' and the DAIR institute are focal points.

niches.name: d/acc & pluralist tech
niches.description: A middle path between e/acc and pause. It wants to speed up defensive, decentralizing and democratic technologies (cryptography, biosecurity, open-source, collective intelligence) rather than all technology or none. Vitalik Buterin's d/acc essays and Weyl and Tang's 'Plurality' are its texts.

niches.name: Forecasters / prediction-market culture
niches.description: People who believe beliefs should be stated as probabilities and tested by markets or forecasting tournaments. It grew from rationalist forecasting (Metaculus) into a mass prediction-market culture (Polymarket, Kalshi) after 2024, and now overlaps with sports betting and political media.

niches.name: Populist AI backlash (anti-transhumanist right & AI-accountability coalition)
niches.description: A cross-partisan political front, loudest on the populist right, that opposes the AI industry's agenda: federal preemption of state AI laws, data-center buildout paid for by ratepayers, AI companions for children and job displacement. Its right wing frames transhumanism as a spiritual threat to human nature; its policy wing works for liability rules, child-safety laws and super PACs that back regulation.

niches.name: Neoreaction & vitalist dissident right
niches.description: An online intellectual subculture inspired by Bronze Age Pervert, Nietzschean 'vitalism', bodybuilding and aesthetic greatness. It is hostile to egalitarianism and 'bugman' modernity and is influential among young right-wing staffers. It overlaps with neoreaction and with raw-food and fitness culture.

niches.name: Progress studies / abundance
niches.description: An intellectual movement that asks why progress happens and why it has slowed, and pushes to remove the barriers that hold it back: permitting, NIMBYism, slow science funding. In 2025 'Abundance' (Klein and Thompson) carried it into center-left politics, while progress-studies institutes kept a nonpartisan, history-of-technology tone.

landmarks.conflict_note: CONFLICT CHECK: reportedly a member of Anthropic's Economic Advisory Council (2025). Not verified in this pass; Benjamin to confirm.

landmarks.name: Pope Leo XIV
landmarks.why: Chose his name partly because of AI and issued the AI encyclical 'Magnifica Humanitas' (2026).
landmarks.added: 2026-11-03 by Benjamin (D-31.18: atlas expansion voices approved)

landmarks.name: Arvind Narayanan
landmarks.why: Princeton computer scientist (with Sayash Kapoor) behind 'AI Snake Oil' and 'AI as Normal Technology', the main rival frame to 'superintelligence soon'.
landmarks.conflict_note: Most works are co-written with Sayash Kapoor; Benjamin may want to add Kapoor as a joint author or as a second person.
landmarks.added: 2026-11-03 by Benjamin (D-31.18: atlas expansion voices approved)

landmarks.name: Andrej Karpathy
landmarks.why: Former OpenAI and Tesla AI lead whose essays and talks ('Software 2.0', 'animals vs ghosts') shape how builders think about LLMs.
landmarks.added: 2026-11-03 by Benjamin (D-31.18: atlas expansion voices approved)
